h1: What are the specific rules and setbacks for building a detached ADU in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Detached ADU Rules: Size, Height, Setbacks and Permits
description: Review Newton's current detached ADU size and setback standards and identify which larger-unit paths require additional approval.
short_answer: Newton allows a new detached ADU by right up to 1,000 square feet or 50% of the principal dwelling's total gross floor area, whichever is smaller. Certain existing accessory structures and owner-occupancy situations may qualify for a detached ADU up to 1,200 square feet, while a detached ADU up to 1,500 square feet requires a special permit. Setbacks and height depend on the local ordinance and building design.

facts.text: Newton's standard by-right detached ADU limit is 1,000 square feet or 50% of the principal dwelling's total gross floor area, whichever is smaller.
Newton identifies qualifying detached ADUs up to 1,200 square feet that may be permitted by right under stated conditions, and detached ADUs up to 1,500 square feet that require a special permit.

qa.q: Can every detached ADU be 1,200 square feet by right?
qa.a: No. Newton lists conditions for the 1,200-square-foot path, including conditions involving an existing accessory structure or owner occupancy. The standard new detached ADU limit is lower.
